key_insight: Transporting eddy centres and re-convolving preserves the spectral envelope, enabling a divergence-free turbulence model with both Richardson pair dispersion and anomalous dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a controlled synthetic-flow framework for studying turbulent particle dispersion and scalar mixing without sacrificing multiscale structure.
method: Construct a spatially defined, divergence-free velocity field on a periodic domain.
Advect eddy-generating centres and re-convolve instead of deforming eddy patterns.
Evaluate pair separation, finite-size Lyapunov scaling and scalar variance budgets.
evidence_signal: The reported sweeping deficit is 0.038 ± 0.019 versus 0.091 ± 0.019 for a frozen field, while the scalar variance budget balances dissipation within 15% over 1.2 decades of scale.
watch_item: Companion proofs apply at small Kubo number; applicability to broader flow regimes and practical engineering geometries remains to be established.
paper_title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
